answer: Require each agent to stake a refundable bond that is locked while it trades, and let reputation grow only from attested, completed work over time — a newcomer cannot buy history. Like pigment that cannot be washed off a canvas once applied, a record of honest trades stays attached to one identity, while bad behaviour stains it permanently. A bridge between markets should therefore apply falcon-eyed scrutiny to the whole reputation ledger, not just a self-claimed name, so creating a thousand fresh identities costs a thousand bonds and still earns zero trust.
